title: boot/01000ms.png and error404/08000ms.png are byte-identical despite different sim states
evidence:
diff --git a/goldens/boot/01000ms.png b/goldens/boot/01000ms.png
index 0000000..c7da635
diff --git a/goldens/error404/08000ms.png b/goldens/error404/08000ms.png
index 0000000..c7da635
10 9ecd87909ca48bb9
80 8480c87e590f11d4
logic_hz 10
detail: Both PNGs resolve to blob c7da635 (byte-identical). At logic_hz 10, boot@1000ms is tick 10 and error404@8000ms is tick 80; those state hashes differ (9ecd87909ca48bb9 vs 8480c87e590f11d4). Deterministic renders of distinct states shouldn't match byte-for-byte.
recommended_fix: Re-capture error404/08000ms.png at tick 80; if it still equals boot's tick-10 frame, the capture pipeline is writing the wrong image or mislabeling the timestamp.

title: boot.log.bin and error404.log.bin share the same git blob
evidence:
diff --git a/goldens/boot.log.bin b/goldens/boot.log.bin
index 0000000..cb7aa8c
diff --git a/goldens/error404.log.bin b/goldens/error404.log.bin
index 0000000..cb7aa8c
detail: Both .log.bin files resolve to blob cb7aa8c (byte-identical), yet error404 runs 250 ticks vs boot's 50 and the .t1 manifests diverge after tick 50. Only harmless if .log.bin is a shared boot/init blob rather than a per-run log.
recommended_fix: Confirm .log.bin semantics: if it is a per-run sim log, regenerate error404.log.bin; if a shared init/boot blob, note that intent so it isn't flagged later.

title: Two PNG capture timestamps exceed their demo's hashed tick window
evidence:
logic_hz 10
ticks 250
index 0000000..1d0e657
logic_hz 10
ticks 3000
index 0000000..dc2310f
detail: At logic_hz 10, error404/40000ms maps to tick 400 (window 250) and surge_basics/305000ms maps to tick 3050 (window 3000). Captures past the hashed sim range risk being empty or stale frames that a render test would trivially pass.
recommended_fix: Confirm whether the ms label is sim-time or wall-clock. If sim-time, retarget these captures to in-range ticks or extend the .t1 hash window to cover them.
